faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.label: Frequently asked questions about CivicLens
faq.languagesAnswer: You can write in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, or mix them. CivicLens is a prototype and its language support is simulated.
faq.category: Do I need to choose a complaint category?
faq.categoryAnswer: No. You can describe the issue in your own words. AI may recommend a category, and a human can review or correct that recommendation.
faq.aiAnswer: The prototype demonstrates how AI could identify language, organise details, estimate urgency, and recommend routing. It does not make final decisions.
faq.decisions: Who decides what happens to my complaint?
faq.decisionsAnswer: People review and make service decisions. AI recommendations include estimated confidence and can be corrected by authorised staff.
faq.incorrectFix: What if the reported fix is not right?
faq.incorrectFixAnswer: A citizen can reject a proposed resolution with a reason. The complaint reopens for further action; only citizen acceptance confirms resolution.
faq.dataSafety: How is my data kept safe?
faq.dataSafetyAnswer: This academic prototype uses mock data and is not a live government service. Do not enter sensitive personal information.

about.title: About CivicLens
about.lead: CivicLens is an academic Final Year Project prototype about multilingual civic complaints in Pakistan.
about.storyTitle: Make civic reports easier to understand, while keeping people in control.
about.missionBody: Explore how multilingual AI could help organise civic complaints and support accountable review without replacing human decisions.
about.problemBody: Residents may describe civic issues in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, or mixed writing. This prototype explores how those reports could be understood and structured for human review.
about.limitsBody: CivicLens is not a live service or an official government portal. AI outputs are simulated recommendations; people remain responsible for decisions.
about.limitsLink: How decisions are made and what the limits are

route.title: Route
route.body: Suggest a responsible department. A person confirms routing before assignment and SLA action.

verify.title: Verify resolution

transparency.title: How decisions are made and what the limits are
transparency.lead: This page explains how recommendations are reviewed by people and describes the boundaries of this academic prototype.

decision.title: AI supports judgement; people make decisions.
decision.body: CivicLens estimates values and recommends routes. It never closes or deletes a complaint.

role.title: What AI does
role.body: AI identifies language, extracts fields, estimates category and urgency, recommends departments, suggests related reports, and adds explainable audit context.

doesNot.title: What AI does not do
doesNot.body: AI does not guarantee outcomes, prove fraud, make an official government determination, automatically resolve cases, or replace human review.

confidence.title: Confidence is an estimate
confidence.body: Confidence values are model estimates, not proof or certainty. Low-confidence results are intended for a human review queue.

human.title: Human override and review queue
human.body: Reviewers can change AI recommendations with a reason. Every override records the AI value, human value, reason, user, and time.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: The append-only trail records AI recommendations and human decisions. There are no edit or delete controls for completed audit entries.

language.title: Languages and Roman Urdu spelling variation
language.body: The prototype explores English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, and mixed text. Roman Urdu spelling varies widely, so the original wording is preserved and normalized text is shown separately.

items.data: Limited Pakistani multilingual training and evaluation data.
items.imbalance: Class imbalance may make common categories appear stronger than uncommon categories.
items.semantic: False semantic matches can connect reports that are not actually related.
items.location: Location accuracy may be limited by vague addresses or text rather than exact coordinates.
items.repairs: Physical repairs are difficult to verify without reliable evidence and citizen confirmation.

privacy.title: Privacy and data minimisation
privacy.body: Collect only fields needed for complaint analysis and review. Keep original wording separate, restrict access by role, and avoid retaining unnecessary data.

modelCard.title: Model-card summary
modelCard.body: Purpose: support multilingual civic complaint analysis. Intended use: recommendations for human review. Inputs: complaint text and optional structured context. Outputs: language, fields, classification, urgency, department recommendation, and review indicators.

synthetic.title: Synthetic-data note
synthetic.label: Clearly labelled synthetic data
synthetic.body: Examples, demo counts, and prototype outputs may use synthetic or illustrative data. They are not measured real-world performance results.
